Queue Management System for SA Government Offices — Design Overview
1. Problem & Goal
Long queues at South African government offices cause wasted time, frustration, and poor customer experience. The goal is to build a WhatsApp + USSD-based digital queue system to:

Allow users to join queues remotely or on-site by entering a queue ID

Provide real-time position and ETA updates

Let admins mark users as served or no-shows

Penalize no-shows by pushing them back exponentially in the queue

Reset queues daily

Improve user experience and reduce physical crowding

2. Core Features
Queue Creation & Reset: Admin creates queue daily, assigned a unique queue ID (e.g., location + date). Queues auto-reset every morning.

User Join: Users join via WhatsApp menu or USSD by entering queue ID.

Queue Position & ETA: System tracks user positions and provides updates every 5 minutes.

Admin Controls: Mark users served, no-show, or remove.

No-Show Penalty: If user misses call, they move back exponentially (2, 4, 8… places).

User Opt-Out: Users can leave the queue anytime.

Alerts: Users get periodic ETA updates and no-show penalties notifications.

3. Technical Architecture
3.1 Storage Choices
Purpose	Storage	Reason
Real-time queue management	Redis	Fast, in-memory, supports lists and atomic ops
Persistent data & logs	SQL DB (Postgres, Supabase) or NoSQL (MongoDB)	Durable storage for history, analytics, admin data

3.2 Redis Queue Structure
Use Redis Lists to store queues:

Key format: queue:{location}:{date}, e.g., queue:homeaffairs_jhb:2025-08-06

List elements: user IDs or phone numbers

Commands:

Add to queue: RPUSH queue_key user_id

Serve next: LPOP queue_key

Get full queue: LRANGE queue_key 0 -1

Set expiry to reset daily: EXPIRE queue_key 86400 (24 hours)

3.3 No-Show Penalty Logic
Track penalties per user in Redis keys, e.g., no_show:{user_id} (number of times no-show)

On no-show:

Remove user from queue (LREM)

Calculate new position = old position + 2^(penalty count)

Reinsert user at new position by rebuilding list (Lua script recommended)

Notify user of penalty and new position

3.4 Avoiding Race Conditions
Multiple simultaneous queue modifications risk race conditions.

Use Redis Lua scripts for atomic remove + reinsert operations.

Alternatively:

Use Redis WATCH + MULTI + EXEC for optimistic locking with retries.

Serialize updates in your app backend to avoid concurrency.

3.5 Estimating Processing Time (ETA)
Take periodic snapshots of queue length:

Store {q_id, timestamp, length} at intervals (e.g., every 5 mins)

Estimate processing speed as:

\text{processing_rate} = \frac{\Delta \text{length}}{\Delta \text{time}}
User ETA = (user position) / processing_rate

Store snapshots in DB or Redis sorted sets

Smooth estimates using multiple snapshots and adjust dynamically

3.6 User Metadata Storage
Use Redis hashes for per-user metadata like status, ETA, joined time:

HSET user_status:{user_id} status waiting eta 12 joined_at 1691300000

Use DB for long-term logs and analytics

4. Tech Stack Recommendations
Redis (self-hosted or managed like Upstash, Redis Cloud)

Database: PostgreSQL or Supabase for persistent data

WhatsApp API: Twilio WhatsApp Business API or alternatives like 360Dialog

USSD Provider: Africa’s Talking or local telco APIs

Backend: Node.js, Python, or Elixir (for concurrency and real-time updates)

Frontend/Admin: React/Vue dashboard for queue management and reporting

5. Summary of Key Redis Commands and Lua Script Concept
Use RPUSH / LPOP for enqueue/dequeue

Use LRANGE to inspect queue

Use LREM + list rebuild in Lua to remove and reposition users atomically

Use TTL (EXPIRE) for daily resets

Store no-show penalty counters in Redis keys

Take snapshots of queue length periodically for ETA calculation

6. Next Steps
Design Redis key schema and Lua scripts for atomic queue updates

Build WhatsApp and USSD menu flows for user interaction

Implement snapshot system for ETA

Build admin dashboard for queue creation, monitoring, and user management

Pilot with one government office or service point
